title: Reading data into R
text:
The data
We use measurements of penguins from three islands. Download the file penguins.csv, and save it in your project folder.



A scatter plot of flipper length against body mass

title: Reading data into R
text:
Read the file
Use read_csv() from the readr package to read the file:
library(readr)
penguins <- read_csv("penguins.csv")

title: Reading data into R
text:
Exercise
How many penguins are in the dataset? And how many columns does it have?






Solution





Use nrow() and ncol():
nrow(penguins)
ncol(penguins)



Want to know more? See the readr documentation.

Introduction to R takes three days. Each day has its own section, with the materials for that day:

Day 1 – Getting started: R and RStudio, and reading your data into R.
Day 2 – Data wrangling: tidy data, and filtering, selecting and reshaping your data.
Day 3 – Plotting: making and customising plots with ggplot2.

Syllabus


Introduction to R


Learn to explore, analyse and visualise your research data with R






Abstract


This training introduces R, a free and widely used programming language for data analysis and statistics. It is designed for researchers who work with data, but have little or no programming experience.
Through short demonstrations and hands-on exercises, you learn how to read data into R, clean and reshape it, summarise it, and create publication-quality plots. You work with real research data throughout, and leave with code you can reuse for your own projects.


Keywords: R · Data analysis · Data visualisation · Reproducible research




Details




Dates


17 May 2027 – 19 May 2027




Duration


3 days




Delivery


In-person




Location


SciLifeLab, Solna




Language


English




Credits


1.5 hpWhether the credits count towards your degree is decided by your own university.






Learning outcomes


After completing this training, participants will be able to:



Use RStudio to write and run R code, and organise your work in projects


Read data from spreadsheet and text files into R


Clean, filter and reshape data with the tidyverse


Summarise data with descriptive statistics


Create and customise plots with ggplot2





Target audience


Researchers and PhD students in the life sciences who want to analyse their own data, with little or no programming experience.


Expertise level: Beginner




Prerequisites




Knowledge



Basic knowledge of statistics, such as means and standard deviations





Technical



Your own laptop, with R and RStudio installed (see Preparation)







Forms of instruction and examination




Forms of instruction



Short lectures and live coding demonstrations


Hands-on exercises with real research data


Group discussions





Forms of examination


Active participation in all sessions, and a short final exercise in which you analyse and plot a dataset of your choice.

Practicalities


Practical information


Everything you need to know to find your way to Introduction to R, and to make the most of your three days in Solna.







Questions about the training?


Get in touch with the training team.

intro-r@example.org




Venue


The training will take place at SciLifeLab Solna in Solna.




Address

Tomtebodavägen 23A171 65 SolnaSweden



Room

Air & Fire (lectures) and the computer room (exercises)



Entrance

Enter through the main entrance, and collect your visitor badge at the reception on the ground floor. Air & Fire is on the ground floor, next to the café. Someone from the team will walk you to the computer room after the first session.








Open map 





Transport


The nearest stops are Karolinska institutet västra (bus) and Solna station (commuter train), both about a ten-minute walk away.



SL, public transport in Stockholm





Accommodation


Accommodation is not included. These hotels are within walking distance of the venue.







Hotel


Distance


Walking time






Hotel Example Solna


600 m


8 minutes




Example Hostel Hagastaden


1.5 km


20 minutes









Food & refreshments


Coffee, tea and fruit are served during the breaks, and lunch is included on all three days.


Tell us about allergies or dietary requirements when you register, or email intro-r@example.org at least one week before the training.




Other information




What to bring


Your own laptop and charger, with R and RStudio installed. See the Preparation page for instructions.




Wi-Fi


Use eduroam if your university has it. Otherwise, ask at the reception for a guest account.
